==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|brāv|a=RP,GA}}, {{IPA|en|/bɹeɪv/}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-brave.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/bɹæɪv/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/bɾev/|[bɾeːv]|a=Scotland}} * {{IPA|en|/bɾeːv/|a=Wales,non-pane-pain}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪv|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{bor|en|frm|brave}}, borrowed from {{der|en|it|bravo}}, itself of uncertain origin (see there). {{doublet|en|bravo}}. ====Adjective==== {{en-adj|er,more}} # Strong in the face of [[fear]]; [[courageous]]. #: {{syn|en|bold|daring|doughty|orped|resilient|stalwart|plucky}} #: {{ant|en|cowardly|fearful|mean|weak}} #* {{RQ:Stoker Dracula|21||Do not fret, dear. You must be '''brave''' and strong, and help me through the horrible task. If you only knew what an effort it is to me to tell of this fearful thing at all, you would understand how much I need your help.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1987|author=Michael Grumley|title=The Last Diary |passage={{...}}he has been so '''brave''', giving it all a dignity.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} Having any sort of [[superiority]] or [[excellence]]. #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=v|page=37|passage=Is it not paſſing '''braue''' to be a King,
And ride in triumph through ''Perſepolis''?}} #* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|chapter=Of Plantations|passage=Iron is a '''brave''' commodity where wood aboundeth.}} #* '''18 February 1666''', {{w|Samuel Pepys}}, ''diary entry'': # Making a fine show or display. #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=ii|page=24|passage=Their plumed helmes are wrought with beaten golde,
Their ſwords enameld, and about their neckes
Hangs maſſie chaines of golde downe to the waſte,
In euery part exceding '''braue''' and rich.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|act=III|scene=iv|passage=Wear my dagger with the '''braver''' grace.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1611|author=John Cooke|title=w:Greene's Tu Quoque |passage=For I have gold, and therefore will be '''brave'''. / In silks I'll rattle it of every color.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1867|author=w:Ralph Waldo Emerson|title=[[s:May-day and other pieces/May-Day|May-Day]] |passage=Frog and lizard in holiday coats / And turtle '''brave''' in his golden spots.}} #* {{RQ:Ferguson Zollenstein|IV |passage=So this was my future home, I thought! Certainly it made a '''brave''' picture. I had seen similar ones fired-in on many a Heidelberg stein. Backed by towering hills,{{...}}a sky of palest Gobelin flecked with fat, fleecy little clouds, it in truth looked a dear little city; the city of one's dreams.}} # {{lb|en|UK|euphemism}} discretion; a bully. #* {{RQ:Dryden Innocence|page=6|passage=Hot '''Braves''', like thee, may fight; but know not well / To manage this, the laſt great Stake of Hell.}} #* {{RQ:Twain Roughing assemblage of two hundred thousand ''young'' men—not simpering, dainty, kid-gloved weaklings, but stalwart, muscular, dauntless young '''braves''', brimful of push and energy, and royally endowed with every attribute that goes to make up a peerless and magnificent manhood—the very pick and choice of the world's glorious ones.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} A challenge; a [[defiance]]; [[bravado]]. #* Online|pos=v|id=9142979828}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[encounter]] or [[withstand]] with courage and [[fortitude]], to [[defy]], to [[provoke]]. #: {{ux|en|After '''braving''' tricks on the high-dive, he '''braved''' a jump off the first diving platform.}} #: {{ux|en|He '''braved''' the storm and spent the night outside. In the morning, he '''braved''' his parents' wrath.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Julius Caesar|IV|3|text=For Cassius is aweary of the world;
Hated by one he loves; '''braved''' by his brother;
Checked like a bondman; all his faults observed,
Set in a notebook, learned, and conned by rote,
To cast into my teeth.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Indian Emperour|passage=The ills of Love, not those of Fate, I fear,
These I can '''brave''', but those I cannot bear {{...}}}} #*: {{...}} but they [Parliament] never will be '''braved''' into it. # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[adorn]]; to make [[fine]] or [[showy]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|IV|3|footer=addressed to a tailor; first use in sense of "adorn", second and third uses in sense of "confront"|text=Face not me. Thou hast '''braved''' many men; '''brave'''
not me.
